decisions: extract_modules.py refuses any new module that reads a name left in the residue, so every assignment here is downward closed: the residue sits at the top of the dependency order and imports its children.

The projectile defence prices from nine of the shared readers, so the map's single extraction is refused. The readers move to interaction_atoms.py, which gives the shape one home for all three interactions rather than a rename that publishes five private names across a module boundary.

The five names the map wanted public (_rank_for, _ability, _ranked_atom_value, _window, _source_selection) are still private and now read across modules. Publish them in the same commit; tests/test_champion_primitives.py reads _window.

Every name read outside interaction_atoms is published, not only the map's five: the four atom queries and _prose_duration_atom cross the same boundary. Two take a new spelling because the bare one is a local variable in both readers: _ability is cached_ability and _window is requested_window. _PROSE_DURATION_QUERIES stays private, read by its own module only.

modules.docstring: The ranked atom and prose duration readers every champion to champion interaction prices from.
One champion to champion interaction with its own eligibility, composition and public shape.
